# Test fixture provenance

Every fixture is generated by `generate-midi0.py` with [mido](https://github.com/mido/mido) 1.3.3 (MIT), run out of process:

```sh
uv run --with mido==1.3.3 python -I tests/fixtures/generate-midi0.py
```

Regenerate rather than hand-edit. The events are synthetic test data written for this repo (MIT); mido is only the oracle.

| File | What | How |
|------|------|-----|
| `type0-melody.mid` | Format 0, 96 ticks per quarter: track name, 3/4, F major, tempo, program change, lyrics, note-offs as both 8n and 9n velocity 0, running status | `mido.MidiFile.save` |
| `type1-ensemble.mid` | Format 1, 480 ticks per quarter, 4 tracks: a conductor track (sequence number, copyright, SMPTE offset, time and key changes, tempo changes with two at one tick, marker, cue point, text), and channel tracks with every channel message, sysex, a program name (meta 08, which mido keeps as an unknown meta message), sequencer-specific and unknown (60) meta events | `mido.MidiFile.save` |
| `type1-ensemble-no-rs.mid` | The same messages without running status | mido's `write_track` with the running-status branch removed, still encoding each message with mido; mido reads it back to the same messages (the generator checks) |
| `type0-merged.mid` | Format 0: `mido.merge_tracks` of `type1-ensemble.mid` | `mido.MidiFile.save` |
| `vlq-and-lengths.mid` | Deltas at every VLQ boundary of the SMF spec table up to `0FFFFFFF`; texts of length 0, 127, 128 and 300, a latin-1 text and one with all 256 byte values; sysex lengths 127 and 128; a 200-byte sequencer-specific event | `mido.MidiFile.save` |
| `smpte-division.mid` | Format 1, SMPTE division -25 fps, 40 ticks per frame (mido keeps it as a negative `ticks_per_beat`), a 29.97 fps SMPTE offset | `mido.MidiFile.save` |
| `type0-empty-track.mid` | Format 0, one track holding only end of track | `mido.MidiFile.save` |
| `type1-no-tracks.mid` | Format 1, no tracks | `mido.MidiFile.save` |
| `midi0-files.sexp` | For each `.mid` above: format, division and every event as mido reads the file back | `mido.MidiFile` |
| `midi0-seconds.sexp` | mido's playback time (`MidiFile` iteration) of every message of the merged tracks of `type0-melody.mid`, `type1-ensemble.mid` and `type0-merged.mid`, as the exact rational value of mido's float | `mido.MidiFile.__iter__` |

## Where the model differs from mido's

The s-expressions are written in the model's terms. The generator maps:

- **Sysex data** keeps the closing `F7` (the model stores the bytes after the length verbatim; mido drops the `F7`).
- **Meta 08** (program name, RP-019) is a `program-name-event`; mido has no class for it and reads an unknown meta message.
- **SMPTE frame rate** 29.97 is written `29`, both in offsets and divisions.
- **Key signatures** are the raw `sf` and `mi` bytes (mido's key names such as `"Cm"`).
- **Pitch bend** is mido's `pitch`, centred on 0.

mido 1.3.3 reads every meta type it has no class for (08 and the unknown ones) with delta 0: `build_meta_message` builds the `UnknownMetaMessage` without the delta it was given. The fixtures and the live test only put such events at delta 0.

Where the readers themselves differ (not exercised by these files): mido sets running status after a sysex event and doesn't skip alien chunks; the model keeps the last channel status across meta, sysex and escape events, and skips alien chunks. The live cross-read test (`mido-reads-what-we-write`) runs the generator with `--dump`, which reads SMFs concatenated on stdin and prints what mido reads.
